issues.title: HALEU deal signed as defense funding shrinks

photo.alt: Gas centrifuges used to enrich uranium
photo.caption: File photo: Gas centrifuges used to enrich uranium.
photo.credit: U.S. Department of Energy, public domain

lines.text: Urenco and Blykalla signed a HALEU enrichment agreement for Blykalla's first SEALER reactor, with deliveries expected in the early 2030s.
Zimbabwe will tax lithium concentrate exports on the value of the lithium sulphate it could produce, not the concentrate's selling price.
Senate appropriators put nearly $9.4 billion for Golden Dome in a draft defense bill, well below the $17.5 billion request.

issues.pro: This week's Pro deep dives cover the HALEU supply chain, Zimbabwe's lithium export tax and the fight over defense reconciliation money.

deepDives.title: Urenco and Blykalla sign HALEU enrichment deal
deepDives.excerpt: Urenco and Blykalla signed an agreement under which uranium feed supplied by Blykalla will be enriched at Urenco's HALEU facility at Capenhurst in the UK. The fuel will be used for Blykalla's first SEALER unit in the USA.

deepDives.title: Zimbabwe changes how it taxes lithium exports
deepDives.excerpt: Zimbabwe will tax lithium concentrate exports based on the value of the lithium sulphate that could be produced from them, not the concentrate's selling price. Finance Minister Mthuli Ncube said benchmark-grade 6% lithium concentrate will be converted at a ratio of five metric tons of concentrate to one ton of lithium sulphate for export tax purposes.

sources.title: Zimbabwe tweaks lithium export tax rule, mandates local sourcing by miners

deepDives.title: Golden Dome funding cut in Senate draft bill
deepDives.excerpt: Senate appropriators pushed roughly half of the administration's $17 billion-plus Golden Dome request into a draft defense bill. The nearly $1.1 trillion proposal from the GOP-led Senate Appropriations Committee tagged nearly $9.4 billion for Golden Dome in its fiscal 2027 defense draft.

sources.title: Appropriators slash Trump’s $17B Golden Dome request in draft bill

issues.title: US funds recycled nuclear fuel projects for advanced reactors

photo.alt: The Beaver Valley nuclear plant, Pennsylvania
photo.caption: File photo: The Beaver Valley nuclear plant, Pennsylvania.
photo.credit: U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission, public domain

lines.text: The US Department of Energy's ARPA-E HORNIG programme awarded funding to Westinghouse, Texas A&M, Standard Nuclear, Oregon State University, Oklo and Exodys Energy for projects that recycle transuranic elements from used fuel into fuel for advanced reactors.
Copper markets are waiting on a US tariff decision, while Grindrod ran its first private test train to Komatipoort and Ivanhoe posted a profitable quarter on record Kamoa-Kakula revenue.
Half of the US Navy's Japan-based destroyers and the carrier George Washington are deployed to Central Command for the war on Iran, pulling assets from the Pacific.

issues.pro: This week's Pro deep dives cover the HORNIG fuel awards, the copper tariff wait and the Pacific naval drawdown.

deepDives.title: US funds projects to recycle used fuel into advanced reactor fuel
deepDives.excerpt: The US Department of Energy's Advanced Research Projects Agency-Energy runs a programme called HORNIG, which opened for applications in April. It funds work to recycle transuranic elements from used nuclear fuel into fuel for advanced reactors.

sources.title: Next-generation fuel projects get US federal funding

deepDives.title: Copper trade waits on a US tariff decision
deepDives.excerpt: BMI reports that the global copper market is awaiting a US tariff decision. Separately, Grindrod ran its first test train to Komatipoort as a private train operating company, with operations to start in 2027.

deepDives.title: Iran war pulls US destroyers from the western Pacific
deepDives.excerpt: Five of the 10 destroyers homeported in Yokosuka, along with the carrier George Washington, are deployed to US Central Command's area of responsibility for the war on Iran. Navy officials have told crews of at least some of those destroyers they won't return home until 2027.
